content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published a document outlining the prerequisites and key action points for the implementation of the Xpert MTB/RIF diagnostic assay at the country level. 1. Legal and Geographic Neutrality: The designations and presentation of material in the publication do not imply any opinion by WHO regarding the legal status of any country, territory, city, or area, nor the delimitation of its borders. Any dotted lines on maps represent approximate boundaries where full agreement may not yet exist. 2. Product Endorsement Disclaimer: The mention of specific companies or products does not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by WHO over other similar products not mentioned. Proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters. 3. Information Verification and Liability: WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information in the publication. However, the material is distributed without any warranty, expressed or implied. The responsibility for interpretation and use of the material lies with the reader, and WHO is not liable for any damages arising from its use. 4. Background on Tuberculosis (TB) Control: Early and improved detection of TB cases, including smear-negative TB often associated with HIV, and expanded capacity to diagnose multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB), are global priorities. The emergence of extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB), institutional transmission, and rapid mortality in MDR-TB and XDR-TB patients with HIV co-infection underscore the need for rapid diagnostic methods. 5. WHO Endorsement of Xpert MTB/RIF: In December 2010, WHO endorsed the Xpert MTB/RIF assay and recommended its phased rollout by national health authorities as part of national plans for managing TB, MDR-TB, and HIV-associated TB. A global consultation convened by WHO in December 2010 achieved consensus on interim diagnostic algorithms, the positioning of Xpert MTB/RIF in risk groups, and programmatic rollout considerations to optimize the technology's use and benefits. 6. Policy Recommendations: Xpert MTB/RIF should be used as the initial diagnostic test for individuals suspected of having MDR-TB or HIV-associated TB (strong recommendation). In settings where MDR-TB or HIV is of lesser concern, Xpert MTB/RIF may be considered a follow-on test to microscopy, particularly for smear-negative specimens (conditional recommendation). Conventional microscopy, culture, and drug susceptibility testing (DST) remain necessary for monitoring treatment progress and detecting resistance to drugs other than rifampicin. In settings where rifampicin resistance is rare, Xpert MTB/RIF results indicating resistance should be confirmed by conventional DST or line probe assay (LPA). 7. Operational Requirements for Implementation: Stable electricity supply and a maximum ambient operating temperature of 30°C for the GeneXpert device. Security measures to prevent theft of the GeneXpert unit and associated equipment. Adequate storage space for cartridges at recommended temperatures (2–28°C). Biosafety precautions similar to those for direct sputum microscopy. Trained personnel with basic computer literacy and knowledge of laboratory registers. Annual calibration of the instrument by a commercial supplier. 8. Checklist of Prerequisites for Country Implementation: Epidemiological Data: Availability of data on MDR-TB and HIV-associated TB prevalence to prioritize placement of the technology and optimize its use in high-risk patient groups. Diagnostic Policy Reform: Plans to modify existing diagnostic algorithms as part of the National TB Program (NTP) strategy to introduce Xpert MTB/RIF testing. Laboratory Network: Existing capacity and referral networks to provide quality-assured laboratory services, including culture and DST for firstand second-line drugs, sputum smear microscopy, and culture for monitoring MDR-TB treatment response. Infrastructure: Stable electricity supply, secure premises, and adequate storage for cartridges. Personnel: Availability of 1–2 trained staff per site to perform testing and maintain equipment. Treatment Capacity: Sufficient capacity for treating identified TB and MDR-TB patients in line with international recommendations. Financing: Secure funding from national budgets or donors. Procurement: Country importation procedures for equipment and consumables, including regulatory registration or waivers. 9. Key Action Points for Implementation: Policy Reform: Incorporate Xpert MTB/RIF testing into NTP diagnostic strategies and algorithms, including identifying appropriate placement within the diagnostic network. Logistics: Identify premises for equipment, allocate storage for cartridges, and establish procedures for cartridge disposal. Procurement: Register the GeneXpert system and Xpert MTB/RIF assay or obtain waivers for importation. Forecast needs, calculate orders, and maintain buffer stock. Financing: Secure sustainable funding to ensure continued use of Xpert MTB/RIF testing. Training: Train staff to perform the assay, ensure timely referral and treatment, and implement infection control measures. Reporting: Adapt reporting forms to include Xpert MTB/RIF results and develop systems for same-day reporting to clinics and regular reporting to WHO. Validation and Maintenance: Use the Global Laboratory Initiative (GLI) validation kit after installation and module calibration. Send modules for annual calibration or after 2,000 tests. 10. Annex: A sample budget is provided to assist countries in planning for the implementation of Xpert MTB/RIF. This document serves as a comprehensive guide for countries to systematically implement the Xpert MTB/RIF assay, ensuring its optimal use and integration into national TB control programs.
